wording_corrections.old: Teach inspection before modelling in two 45-minute sessions. Use fictional data only. Emphasize the unit of observation, provenance, units, unknown values and overlapping audit flags. The dataset card is a concise classroom documentation exercise inspired by datasheets for datasets, not a claim to implement every part of a research framework. Students must distinguish observations from unsupported repairs and from evidence of model fitness.
wording_corrections.new: Use the three-session route to build a card from complete supplied fictional facts, distinguish unknown fields, and version a condition/count update. Earlier trip-audit material remains review. A card records evidence and questions; it does not certify quality, permission or model performance.

wording_corrections.old: It is a numerical quantity whose differences measure time. Whole-number formatting does not turn it into a category.
wording_corrections.new: Retain original source and group IDs, exact assignments, intended prediction claim, label version and training-only preprocessing fit. A source record can document these without claiming that evaluation has happened.

wording_corrections.old: Use the worked case for Dataset inspection and cards. Proposed explanation: “A complete card certifies data quality”. Decide whether this explanation is supported. Point to the step or supplied fact that decides; explain your repair if needed.
wording_corrections.new: A dataset card has every heading filled, but each unknown field was guessed. Does completeness establish that its claims are correct or that a model is ready? Name the repair.

wording_corrections.old: The card records evidence and gaps; its claims still need checking. Documentation does not prove suitability.
wording_corrections.new: No. Replace unsupported entries with explicit unknowns and questions, cite supplied evidence, retain versions and perform the missing checks; formatting completeness is not validation.

wording_corrections.new: Offer blank card headings and the exact source brief; prompt learners to label entries given, unknown or proposed. Extension: require a revision record with old/new counts, unchanged plant IDs and unresolved metadata.

wording_corrections.old: Require W4 counts 6,5,2,1,1 in the stated order, the Q overlap, acceptance of zero under this schema, and a card with source, unit, raw version and excluded use. Fresh retry: rows (L,3), (M,None), (N,-2), (N,-2), (O,0). Counts are 5 raw, 4 IDs, 1 missing, 2 negative and 1 extra ID occurrence. The negative and repeated-ID flags overlap on N. Do not infer whether the two N rows describe one event without checking the source.

Source creator/date/permission and other unsupplied fields remain unknown; require a proposed target/rule and plant grouping without claiming completed evaluation. wording_corrections.new: Next is Week10: Baselines First. Carry forward the versioned card, source groups, label contract and intended use so every baseline result names its data and evaluation context. Research reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010 (Datasheets for Datasets).
